actions.operation: Change the link-arm profile to a long-hole shape.

parameters.interpreted_geometry: External closed obround/capsule profile spanning the two terminal pivot axes of each link arm
parameters.profile_application: Apply consistently to all four linkage plates while preserving their existing pivot-axis locations and 2 mm plate thickness

actions.target: The profile of the link arms.
actions.relational_constraint: The resulting profile must have the shape of a long hole. Because the stated intention is to increase stiffness, 'long hole shape' is localized as an external obround link-arm envelope rather than a new internal elongated cutout. The two terminal pivot centers define the obround centerline and rounded ends, while the central pivot remains on the link centerline.
actions.unresolved_reference: The exact external obround width, rounded-end radius, and required stiffness increase are not specified. Preserve at least the existing maximum material envelope around the pivot bosses and do not reduce the minimum ligament around any bore.
steps: Localize the affected components as the four repeated linkage plates in section R03: F007 in SOLID 0, F009 in SOLID 8, F011 in SOLID 9, and F013 in SOLID 10. Do not alter the support-platform bodies R01/R02 or the pivot-pin solids R04 for this profile operation.

Use a broad planar face normal to CAD Z as the sketch reference for each plate: FACE 12 or FACE 24 for F007, FACE 142 or FACE 154 for F009, FACE 171 or FACE 183 for F011, and FACE 200 or FACE 212 for F013.

For each descending plate, construct a sketch centerline through the upper-left and lower-right terminal pivot centers. For each ascending plate, construct a centerline through the lower-left and upper-right terminal pivot centers. Preserve the original terminal and central pivot coordinates and constrain the central pivot center to the corresponding link centerline.

Replace the existing narrow web and localized circular-boss outer boundary with one continuous external obround profile. Create equal-radius end arcs centered on the two terminal pivot axes and connect them with two tangent, parallel side lines.

Dimension the obround width so that it is no smaller than the existing maximum boss diameter and so that the minimum radial material ligament around the terminal and central bores is preserved or increased. Use a shared parameter for the obround half-width to keep all four repeated plates consistent.
Retain the three original coaxial through-bore locations in every link plate. The profile change must not move the lower, upper, or central articulation axes.

Extrude or rebuild the closed obround sketch normal to CAD Z to the existing 2.0 mm plate thickness and at the original Z placement of each solid. Preserve the separated positive-Z and negative-Z linkage layers.
Apply the same parameterized profile to the parallel plate pairs F007/F011 and F009/F013, using mirroring or a repeated-feature definition where practical.
Recreate only small edge blends required to match the original manufacturing treatment. Avoid large fillets that reduce the designed ligament near the bores.

Check the assembly through its motion range for collisions between the wider obround arms, the opposite crossed arm, the upper and lower platforms, and adjacent linkage layers. Verify that the modified arms remain separate solids and retain the original pivot axes.

actions.operation: Change the diameter of the holes.
actions.target: The three pivot holes in each of the four link arms.
actions.relational_constraint: Perform this action after changing the link-arm profile. Keep all twelve bore centers and their CAD-Z axes unchanged and apply the same diameter change to the repeated linkage-plate bore sets F008, F010, F012, and F014. The platform guide slots and platform fixed-pivot holes are excluded because the grammatical reference follows 'link arms' and the stiffness-related profile edit.
actions.unresolved_reference: The direction of the 1 mm diameter change is not explicitly stated. The original linkage bores are 5.0 mm in diameter and the mating pins are 4.8 mm in diameter. A decrease to 4.0 mm would interfere with the existing pins, whereas an increase to 6.0 mm would retain assembly clearance; therefore increasing to 6.0 mm is the functionally preferred interpretation, but the direction should be confirmed before final manufacture.
steps: Edit the circular cut definitions belonging to the four linkage bore sets: F008, F010, F012, and F014. These features contain the central and two terminal holes in each plate.

Use the existing cylindrical bore walls as localization references: FACE 25, FACE 26, and FACE 27 for F008; FACE 155, FACE 156, and FACE 157 for F010; FACE 184, FACE 185, and FACE 186 for F012; and FACE 213, FACE 214, and FACE 215 for F014.
Preserve every existing bore center and maintain all bore axes parallel to CAD Z. Do not reposition any pivot center while changing its diameter.
Define a common bore-diameter parameter d_link. Set d_link to 6.0 mm if the requested 1 mm change means an increase, or to 4.0 mm if it means a decrease.

Prefer the 6.0 mm interpretation because all existing pivot pins have a 4.8 mm diameter. A 6.0 mm bore produces 1.2 mm diametral clearance, while a 4.0 mm bore cannot receive the current pins and would require an additional pin redesign not requested.
Cut the revised circles through the full 2.0 mm thickness of each linkage plate. Apply the same value to all twelve link-arm bores to preserve repeated-part consistency.

Do not change the lower platform slot walls FACE 72, FACE 73, FACE 78, and FACE 80; the upper platform slot walls FACE 111, FACE 112, FACE 117, and FACE 119; or the platform fixed-bores FACE 79 and FACE 118 unless a later requirement explicitly requests matching platform-interface changes.

Do not change the pin bearing surfaces FACE 30, FACE 38, FACE 121, FACE 126, FACE 35, and FACE 218 under this action. Validate the resulting bore-to-pin clearance against the intended fit and bearing-load requirement.
Regenerate the four plate solids and confirm that each modified bore remains fully enclosed by the adjusted obround profile with no breakout or insufficient ligament.

actions.operation: Adjust the referenced shape to accommodate the hole-diameter change.

parameters.adjustment_rule: Preserve or increase the original minimum radial ligament from each revised link-arm bore to the external obround boundary
parameters.preferred_diameter_case: For a 1 mm bore-diameter increase, increase the local outer radius or obround width by at least 1 mm overall, equivalent to 0.5 mm per side, unless the profile created in the first action already provides a larger ligament
parameters.stiffness_constraint: Do not reduce the obround width in response to a bore decrease because that would conflict with the stiffness intention

actions.target: The new external obround profiles of all four linkage plates around their terminal and central pivot holes.
actions.relational_constraint: The adjustment must correspond to the 1 mm hole-diameter change. Maintain the original pivot centers, plate thickness, crossed-link arrangement, and positive-Z/negative-Z repetition. The modified external shape must preserve adequate material around every changed bore and must not reduce link-arm stiffness.
actions.unresolved_reference: No required minimum edge distance, bearing-area criterion, material, load, or manufacturing standard is supplied. Use the original radial ligament as the minimum geometric baseline and confirm the final dimensions by structural and bearing-stress calculations.
steps: After setting the revised bore diameter, calculate the original minimum radial ligament between each 5.0 mm bore and the existing outer link boundary.

Parameterize the new obround end radius as R_outer = d_link/2 + t_ligament, where t_ligament is not less than the original minimum radial ligament. Apply the same governing ligament to both terminal rounded ends.

Set the distance between the two parallel obround side lines so that the central bore has at least the same ligament as the terminal bores. If the central hole governs, increase the full obround width accordingly.

For the functionally preferred increase from 5.0 mm to 6.0 mm, offset each obround side and rounded end outward by at least 0.5 mm relative to a profile designed around the original bores, unless the first profile operation already supplies that additional material.

If a decrease to 4.0 mm is explicitly confirmed together with compatible smaller pins, retain the stiffer obround envelope rather than shrinking it; this increases the available ligament and remains consistent with the stiffness intention.
Maintain tangency between the straight side segments and rounded ends, and keep the external profile symmetric about each link centerline.
Regenerate all four linkage plates using the shared profile and bore parameters. Preserve the original 2.0 mm thicknesses and Z-layer positions.

Inspect for minimum edge distance, bore breakout, self-intersection, and excessive local curvature. Verify that no adjusted profile contacts the platforms or the crossing link throughout the intended articulation range.

Perform a final assembly-fit check with the existing 4.8 mm pins and a structural check for axial compression, secondary bending, and bearing stress around the enlarged holes. Increase the obround width further if the stiffness or bearing criteria are not met.
